questions.question: What does a Gaussian process prior describe?
options: A distribution over possible functions
One fixed polynomial selected before seeing data
A lookup table whose uncertainty is always zero
A classifier boundary that cannot represent regression
questions.explanation: A GP prior assigns a joint Gaussian distribution to every finite set of function values.

questions.question: What does the RBF length scale control?
options: The number of observations stored
How quickly correlation falls with input distance
The target's measurement unit only
The Cholesky algorithm's loop count regardless of matrix size
questions.explanation: Short length scales allow faster variation; long length scales correlate points over larger distances.

questions.question: Why use Cholesky solves instead of an explicit covariance inverse?
options: They remove the need for a kernel
They guarantee the model is correctly specified
They are more numerically stable for positive-definite systems
They make posterior variance independent of observations
questions.explanation: Triangular solves avoid forming an explicit inverse and expose factorization failures clearly.

questions.question: Where should posterior variance usually be smallest under a smooth kernel?
options: Infinitely far from every input
Near well-observed training inputs
At a randomly chosen plot boundary
Everywhere equally after a single measurement
questions.explanation: Conditioning reduces uncertainty most strongly near informative observations.

questions.question: What does high marginal likelihood establish?
options: The model will be correct on every future domain
The kernel is legally safe to deploy
No held-out evaluation is needed
The setting balances data fit and covariance complexity within the assumed model
questions.explanation: Marginal likelihood compares settings under the chosen GP assumptions; it does not validate those assumptions on its own.

questions.question: What is the best response to conflicting duplicate inputs?
options: Model observation noise and inspect conditioning
Silently delete the target with the larger magnitude
Set all posterior variances to zero
Increase length scale until every function becomes constant
questions.explanation: Explicit noise represents conflicting measurements and bounded jitter handles only numerical conditioning.
